overview.title: Another Layer of Fes
overview.p1: The Mellah was established in the 15th century as the Jewish quarter of Fes, next to the royal palace in Fes el-Jdid. For centuries it was a lively neighbourhood of merchants and craftspeople, and it preserves a distinctive chapter of Moroccan Jewish history.
overview.p2: What stands out is the architecture: houses with balconies that face the street, unlike the inward-looking homes of the medina. Walk the main street, then visit the restored Ibn Danan synagogue and the Jewish cemetery, and combine it with the gilded gates of the Royal Palace nearby. Check locally which sites are open and their entry fees.

moods.title: What to See in the Mellah
moods.subtitle: Architecture, heritage and a quieter side of Fes.

1.title: Balconied Streets
1.desc: Wooden balconies and shutters face the street, a striking contrast with the medina's inward houses.

2.title: Ibn Danan Synagogue
2.desc: A restored synagogue that offers a look at Fes's Jewish heritage. Check opening times and entry locally.

3.title: The Jewish Cemetery
3.desc: Rows of whitewashed tombs on a hillside make a quiet, moving stop. Be respectful and modest.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Fes Mellah

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: The Mellah is in Fes el-Jdid, reached by petit taxi or on foot from Bab Bou Jeloud in about 30 to 40 minutes. It pairs well with the Royal Palace gates.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Go in the morning or afternoon. Some shops and sites close on Friday and Saturday, so check before you go.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: Dress modestly, be respectful at the cemetery and synagogue, and ask before photographing people. Carry some cash for entry fees.

q1.question: What is the Mellah?
q1.answer: The historic Jewish quarter of Fes, set up in the 15th century beside the royal palace in Fes el-Jdid.

q2.question: What can I see in the Mellah?
q2.answer: The balconied main street, the restored Ibn Danan synagogue and the Jewish cemetery.

q3.question: Is the Mellah free to visit?
q3.answer: Walking the streets is free. Some individual sites, like the synagogue, may charge admission.

q4.question: How long should I spend there?
q4.answer: One to two hours covers the streets, the synagogue and the cemetery.
